Even if you, sir, argue a hundred times,
he still will not listen.
You, sir, should rather use Yí’s words as leverage and return to the King of Chǔ.”
Chén Zhěn said: “Good.”
He then sent someone to speak first to the King of Chǔ.
Zhāng Yí wanted to corner Chén Zhěn,
so he had the King of Wèi summon him to serve as chancellor,
intending to trap him when he came.
As he was about to depart,
his son Chén Yìng stopped his father from going,
saying: “When things are murky,
one cannot fail to examine them carefully.
When Zhèng Qiáng left Qín, he said
Yìng understood.
Now Wèi wishes to sever relations between Chǔ and Qí,
so they will certainly warmly welcome you, sir.
Those in Yǐngzhōng who dislike you, sir,
wishing for your departure,
will certainly urge the king to provide you with many carriages.
When you, sir, reach Sòng,
claim illness on the road and do not proceed.
Send someone to tell the King of Qí:
‘The reason Wèi welcomed me
was to sever relations between Qí
and Chǔ.’”
The King of Qí said:
“If you, sir, indeed do not go to Wèi but come to see me instead,
I will grant you a fief.”
He then sent the carriage of the Marquis of Lǔ to welcome him.
Zhāng Yí fled to Wèi,
and Wèi was about to welcome him.
Zhāng Chǒu advised the king,
wishing not to admit him,
but failed to persuade the king.
Zhāng Chǒu withdrew
and again advised the king, saying:
“Has Your Majesty heard of the old concubine serving her mistress?
When her children have grown and her beauty faded,
she only cares for the household.
Now my service to Your Majesty
is like that old concubine serving her mistress.”
The King of Wèi then did not admit Zhāng Yí.
Zhāng Yí wanted to ally Wèi with Qín and Hán to attack Qí and Chǔ.
Huì Shī wanted to ally Wèi with Qí and Chǔ to halt military action.
Many spoke in favor of Master Zhāng before the king.
Huìzǐ said to the King:
"This is a minor matter,
yet those who say it can be done and those who say it cannot are evenly split.
How much more so for a major affair?
To ally Wèi with Qín and Hán to attack Qí and Chǔ,
this is a major affair,
yet all of Your Majesty's ministers consider it feasible.
I do not know if its feasibility
is as clear as this?
Or if the ministers' understanding of statecraft
is as uniform as this?
If its feasibility
is not so clear,
and the ministers' understanding of statecraft
is also not all the same,
then half the channels are blocked.
What is called 'coercing the ruler'
is losing that half."
Zhāng Zǐyí (Zhang Yi) became the Prime Minister of Wèi on behalf of Qín,
causing Qí and Chǔ to become angry and wish to attack Wèi.
Yōng Jǔ said to Zhāngzǐ:
"The reason Wèi made you, sir, its Prime Minister
is that with you as Prime Minister, the state would be secure,
and the common people would have no troubles.
Now, with you as Prime Minister, Wèi is subjected to military attack.
This means Wèi's plan was mistaken.
If Qí and Chǔ attack Wèi,
you, sir, will certainly be in danger."
Zhāngzǐ said:
"What, then, should be done?"
Yōng Jǔ said: "I request to make Qí and Chǔ call off their attack."
Yōng Jǔ said to the rulers of Qí and Chǔ:
"Has Your Majesty also heard of Zhāng Yí's pact with the King of Qín?
He said:
'If Your Majesty appoints Yí as Prime Minister of Wèi,
Qí and Chǔ, detesting Yí,
will certainly attack Wèi.
If Wèi fights and wins,
then the armies of Qí and Chǔ will be broken,
and Yí will firmly control Wèi;
if they do not defeat Wèi,
Wèi will certainly serve Qín to maintain its state,
and will surely cede territory to bribe Your Majesty.
If they then wish to attack again,
their exhaustion will leave them unable to withstand Qín.'
This is the secret agreement Yí made with the King of Qín.
Now, if you attack Wèi while Yí is its Prime Minister,
you are making Yí's scheme come true for Qín.
This is not the way to thwart Yí."
The kings of Qí and Chǔ said: "Good."
Thereupon they immediately called off the attack on Wèi.
Zhāng Yí wanted to be Prime Minister of both Qín and Wèi simultaneously.
Therefore, he said to the King of Wèi:
"I, Yí, request that Qín attack Sānchuān.
Your Majesty, seize the opportunity to seize Nányáng by agreement.
The Hán clan will then perish."
Shǐ Yàn said to Zhào Xiàn:
"Why don't you, sir, use Chǔ to assist Yí in seeking the premiership in Wèi?
Hán, fearing destruction,
will certainly flee south to Chǔ.
If Yí concurrently serves as Prime Minister of Qín and Wèi,
then you, sir, will certainly also concurrently serve as Prime Minister of Chǔ and Hán."
The King of Wèi was about to make Zhāng Yí his Prime Minister.
Xīshǒu (the Marquess of Zhi), seeing no benefit for himself,
therefore sent someone to say to Hán Gōngshū:
"Zhāng Yí has already allied Qín and Wèi.
His words are:
'If Wèi attacks Nányáng,
and Qín attacks Sānchuān,
the Hán clan will certainly perish.'
Moreover, the reason the King of Wèi values Zhāngzǐ
is his desire to obtain territory.
Then Hán's Nányáng will be taken.
Why don't you, sir, cede a small portion of it,
attributing it as an achievement for Yǎn (Xīshǒu),
so that the alliance between Qín and Wèi can be broken?
If this is done,
then Wèi will certainly scheme against Qín and abandon Yí,
ally with Hán and make Yǎn its Prime Minister."
Gōngshū believed it to be true,
and accordingly ceded the territory.
Xīshǒu took credit for it,
and indeed became Prime Minister of Wèi.
Chǔ promised Wèi six cities to join in attacking Qí and preserving Yān.
Zhāng Yí wanted to ruin this plan.
He said to the King of Wèi:
"Qí, fearing the alliance of the three states,
will certainly return Yān's territory to appease Chǔ.
Chǔ and Zhào will certainly agree to this,
and will not give Wèi the six cities.
This means Your Majesty will have failed in your schemes with Chǔ and Zhào,
and will have incurred enmity from Qí and Qín.
Qí will then attack Zhào,
take Chéngqiū,
and recover its invaded territory.
Xū and Dùnqiū will be endangered.
Chǔ will crush Nányáng and Jiǔyí,
enter Pèi,
and Xǔ and Yānlíng will be endangered.
What Your Majesty will obtain
is only Xīnguān.
Yet the roads pass through Sòng and Wèi, which control them.
If the affair fails, you will have driven [the outcome] for Zhào;
if it succeeds, the fruits will hang with Sòng and Wèi."
The King of Wèi did not listen.
Zhāng Yí informed Gōng Zhòng,
instructing him, using the famine as a reason,
to entice the King of Hán with territory near Héwài.
The King of Wèi became fearful
and asked Zhāngzǐ.
Zhāngzǐ said:
"Qín wants to rescue Qí.
Hán wants to attack Nányáng.
Qín and Hán joining forces to attack Nányáng
makes no difference.
Moreover, use the meeting to divine Your Majesty's fortune.
If Your Majesty does not meet with Qín,
Hán's divination is decided."
The King of Wèi then agreed to meet with Q
He said to the King of Qí:
"Your Majesty made an alliance with the three states to exclude Wèi.
Now Wèi has sent Gōngsūn Yǎn here,
and you have been talking with him for a long time.
This means Your Majesty is scheming against the three states."
The King of Qí said:
"When the King of Wèi heard of my arrival,
he sent Gōngsūnzǐ to greet me.
I did not discuss anything with him."
The three states did not trust the King of Qí's meeting,
and the affair thus failed.
Wèi ordered Gōngsūn Yǎn to seek peace with Qín.
Qímǔ Huī taught him what to say:
"Do not cede too much territory.
Say that
if peace is achieved,
Qín will certainly value the peace
and meet with the king;
if peace is not achieved,
then in the future, no one will be able
to bring Wèi into alliance with Qín."
Gōngsūn Yǎn served as a general of Wèi,
but did not get along with the chancellor Tián Xū.
Jìzǐ spoke to the King of Liáng on Yǎn's behalf:
"Has Your Majesty not seen oxen harnessed alongside thoroughbreds?
They cannot travel a hundred paces.
Now Your Majesty considers Yǎn capable of leading armies,
and therefore employs him;
yet you follow the chancellor's plans.
This is like harnessing oxen with thoroughbreds.
Both ox and horse will perish,
and the task will not be accomplished.
Your Majesty's state will surely suffer harm!
I hope Your Majesty will consider this."
Xīshǒu and Tián Pàn wanted to obtain troops from Qí and Wèi to attack Zhào,
but the Lord of Liáng and the Marquis of Tián were unwilling.
Xīshǒu said:
"I request fifty thousand men from each state,
and within five months Zhào will be destroyed."
Tián Pàn said:
"Those who lightly employ their troops
endanger their state;
those who easily adopt stratagems
bring themselves to ruin.
Now you speak of destroying Zhào with such ease,
I fear there will be later calamity."
Xīshǒu said:
"You lack wisdom.
Those two rulers
are already unwilling.
Now you speak of difficulties to frighten them,
so that Zhào will not be attacked,
and the plans of us two will be thwarted.
Moreover, if you speak bluntly of ease,
the opportunity will already be lost.
If difficulties arise and troops are engaged,
when the Marquis of Tián and the Lord of Liáng see the danger,
how would they dare withhold troops and not give them to us?"
Tián Pàn said:
"Excellent."
He then urged both rulers to heed Xīshǒu.
Xīshǒu
and Tián Pàn thus obtained the troops of Qí and Wèi.
Before the troops crossed the border,
the Lord of Liáng and the Marquis of Tián, fearing they would arrive and be defeated in battle,
mobilized all their forces to follow them,
and inflicted a major defeat on the Zhào clan.
Xīshǒu met with the Lord of Liáng and said:
"I exhaust my strength and wisdom,
seeking to expand Your Majesty's territory and win you honor.
Yet Tián Xū undermines you from within,
and Your Majesty listens to him,
so that I can never achieve success.
If Xū leaves, I will remain;
if Xū remains, I request to leave."
The king said:
"Xū is a minister close to me.
For your inconvenience,
to kill him or drive him away—
what would the world say?
And how would the ministers at court react?
Now for your sake, I will keep him outside,
ordering him not to dare interfere in your affairs.
If anyone interferes in your affairs,
I will kill or banish them for you.
How is that?"
Xīshǒu agreed.
Thereupon he went east to meet Tián Yīng,
and formed an alliance with him;
summoned Wénzǐ to serve as chancellor of Wèi,
while he himself became chancellor of Hán.
Sū Dài spoke to the King of Wèi on behalf of Tián Xū:
"I venture to ask: when Wénzǐ serves Wèi,
how does it compare to when he served Qí?"
The king said:
"It is not as good as when he served Qí."
"When Yǎn serves Wèi,
how does it compare to when he serves Hán?"
The king said:
"It is not as good as when he serves Hán."
Sū Dài then said:
"Yǎn will favor Hán over Wèi,
and Wénzǐ will favor Qí over Wèi.
These two men
will employ Your Majesty's state
to undertake affairs in the world.
If halfway through it becomes unfeasible,
Your Majesty may not even hear of it.
Though Your Majesty's state may be drained and troubled, they will follow their course.
Your Majesty should rather keep Xū by your side,
to monitor the actions of these two men.
The two men will say:
'Xū is not one of us;
if we undertake affairs detrimental to Wèi,
Xū will surely undermine us before the king.'
Thus, the two men will not dare harbor disloyal intentions.
Whether the actions of these two men
benefit Wèi or not,
if Your Majesty places Xū by your side to monitor them,
I believe it will benefit you personally
and facilitate state affairs."
The king said:
"Excellent."
He indeed placed Xū by his side.
Shǐ Jǔ spoke against Xīshǒu before the king.
Xīshǒu wanted to corner him,
so he said to Zhāng Yí:
"I will ask the king to offer the state to you, sir.
Then the king will be like Yáo and Shùn;
and if you, sir, decline,
you will be like Xǔ Yóu.
I will then ask the king
to grant you a fief of ten thousand households."
Zhāng Yí was pleased,
and thus had Shǐ Jǔ frequently visit Xīshǒu.
When the king heard of this, he did not employ Shǐ Jǔ,
who then left without taking leave.
The King of Chǔ attacked the south of Liáng, and Hán took the opportunity to besiege it.
Chéng Huī spoke to the King of Hán on behalf of Xīshǒu:
"Attack Qiáng swiftly,
and the Chǔ army will surely advance.
Wèi will be unable to withstand,
and will submit to Chǔ.
Hán will then be in danger,
so Your Majesty should abandon the siege of Qiáng.
With Hán no longer a threat,
Wèi will certainly fight Chǔ.
If they are defeated,
they will be unable to defend Dàliáng, let alone hold Qiáng.
If they win the battle,
their troops will be exhausted,
and Your Majesty's attack on Qiáng will be easy."
When King Huì of Wèi died,
the burial date was set.
Heavy snow fell,
accumulating up to the eyes of oxen,
damaging the city walls,
and they had to build a plank road for the burial.
Many ministers advised the crown prince,
saying:
"To proceed with the funeral in such heavy snow
will surely cause the people great hardship.
Moreover, the official expenses may be insufficient.
We request to postpone the date."
The crown prince said:
"As a son,
to delay the funeral of the former king
due to the people's labor and official expenses
would be unrighteous.
Say no more."
The ministers dared not speak further,
and informed Xīshǒu. Xīshǒu said:
"I have no way to speak of this;
only Lord Huì can do so.
Please inform Lord Huì."
Duke Huì said:
"Very well."
He rode in his carriage to see the Crown Prince and said:
"The burial date has been set."
The Crown Prince said:
"Indeed."
Duke Huì said:
"In the past, King Jìlì was buried at the foot of Chǔ Mountain.
The Luàn River eroded his tomb,
exposing the front end of his coffin.
King Wén said:
'Alas!
Our former lord must wish to see his ministers and the common people once more,
and thus caused the Luàn River to reveal it.'
Thereupon, the coffin was brought out and displayed at court,
where all the common people saw it,
and after three days it was reburied.
This was the righteous act of King Wén.
Now the burial date has been set,
but the snow is very heavy,
reaching up to the eyes of oxen,
making travel difficult.
If Your Highness, for the sake of keeping to the date,
would you not be suspected of wanting to rush the burial?
I wish Your Highness would change the date.
Our former king must wish to linger a while to support the altars of state and pacify the black-haired people,
and thus caused the snow to be so heavy.
Therefore, postpone the date and choose another.
This would be the righteous act of King Wén.
If you do not act thus,
does it mean you are ashamed to emulate King Wén?"
The Crown Prince said:
"Excellent.
I respectfully postpone the date,
and will choose another."
Master Huì not only carried out his persuasion,
but also caused the Crown Prince of Wèi, before burying his former king,
to thereby be persuaded of the righteousness of King Wén.
Persuading others of the righteousness of King Wén to show the world,
was this a minor achievement?
The five states attacked Qín but returned without success.
Afterward,
Qí wanted to attack Sòng,
but Qín prevented it.
Qí sent Sòng Guǒ to Qín,
to request an alliance to attack Sòng.
The King of Qín agreed.
The King of Wèi, fearing an alliance between Qí and Qín,
wanted to make peace with Qín.
He said to the King of Wèi:
"The King of Qín said to Sòng Guǒ:
'The ones who will divide Sòng's cities
and subdue Sòng's strongholds
are the six states.
Those who will exploit Sòng's weakness
and contend with Your Majesty for gains
are Chǔ and Wèi.
I ask Your Majesty not to prevent Chǔ from attacking Wèi,
and Your Majesty alone can take Sòng.
When Your Majesty attacks Sòng,
I ask that you use both firmness and gentleness.
As for a state like Sòng,
to deceive it is not wrong,
to kill its people does not make enemies.
Your Majesty should not negotiate with it to obtain territory;
after having obtained territory,
use force to attack it,
aiming only to devour Sòng.'
"I have heard these words,
and secretly grieve for Your Majesty,
for Qín will surely use this against Your Majesty.
It will surely also demand territory from Your Majesty, and after obtaining territory, will again use force to attack Your Majesty.
It will surely also tell Your Majesty to make you despise Qí,
and when relations between Qí and Wèi have soured,
it will then ally with Qí to make further demands on Your Majesty.
Qín has used this against Chǔ before,
and also used it against Hán before.
I hope Your Majesty will consider this deeply.
Qín's goodwill toward Wèi is unfathomable.
Therefore, for Your Majesty's plan,
the best is to attack Qín,
next is to alienate Qín,
next is to strengthen alliances
and pretend to negotiate peace,
without separating from your allied states.
If Qín and Qí unite,
our state will be untenable.
I hope Your Majesty will listen to me,
and must not negotiate peace.
"Qín's power weighs heavily on Wèi;
Wèi, having twice shown its wisdom,
therefore, those who would harm Qín for you,
dare not act openly.
If the world can be ordered to attack Qín,
they will secretly encourage it but dare not plot openly.
When they see the world harming Qín,
they will first betray their allies to extricate themselves.
If the world can be ordered to alienate Qín,
they will be coerced by their allies
and act out of necessity.
If the world will not,
they will be the first to leave,
and make Qín their closest ally to enhance their own status.
Such men
use Your Majesty as capital,
so how can they save the state from peril?
Those who would save the state from peril
must exhaust the three strategies,
and implement the highest.
If the highest is not possible,
then implement the middle;
if the middle is not possible,
then implement the lowest;
if the lowest is not possible,
then clearly refuse to ally with Qín.
And while alive, work to weaken Qín,
causing Qín to have neither a hundred grievances nor a hundred benefits,
but only to consider its own safety.
If you, my lord, can sell this plan to ally with Qín,
this is the strategy to save the state from peril.
How could I be worthy of it?
Nevertheless,
I hope you will consider my plan.
"Yān and Qí are enemy states;
Qín is a brotherly ally.
To unite with an enemy state to attack a marital ally,
I find bitter.
When Huángdì fought on the plains of Zhuōlù,
the armies of the Western Róng did not come;
when Yǔ attacked the Sānmiáo,
the people of the Eastern Yí
did not rise.
To use Yān to attack Qín,
even Huángdì would find difficult,
yet I have caused Yān's armor to be raised and Qí's troops to march.
"I have also extensively served the officials of the Three Jìn,
Fèngyáng Jūn, Mèngcháng Jūn, Hán Mǐn,
Zhōu Zuì, Zhōu, Hán Yúwéi,
and their followers, bringing them under my influence,
fearing their suspicion about attacking Qín.
I have also personally made myself odious to Qín:
the one who proposed burning all the Qín tallies in the world
was I;
the one who next transmitted the agreement to burn the tallies
was I;
the one who wanted to make the five states agree to close the passes against Qín
was I.
Fèngyáng Jūn and Hán Yúwéi have already made peace;
Sū Xiū and Zhū Yīng are both secretly in Hándān;
I also persuaded the King of Qí
and went to undermine them.
When the world was negotiating peace together,
I had Sū Xiū spread word throughout the world,
and made Qí the closest ally,
then troops were requested to attack Wèi,
and I again argued against it at the risk of death.
And indeed, later, through Sū Xiū, a weighty report came from the west.
I am not unaware of the weight of Qín's power,
but the reason I acted thus
was for you, my lord."
Wèi Wénzǐ, Tián Xū, and Zhōu Xiāo were on good terms,
and wanted to incriminate Xī Shǒu.
Xī Shǒu was troubled by this,
and said to the King of Wèi:
"What we should worry about now
is Qí.
Yīngzǐ's words and deeds influence the King of Qí.
If Your Majesty wants to win over Qí,
then why not summon Wénzǐ and make him chancellor?
He will surely devote himself to making Qí serve Your Majesty."
The King said:
"Good."
Thereupon, he summoned Wénzǐ and made him chancellor.
Thus, Xī Shǒu betrayed Tián Xū and Zhōu Xiāo.
The King of Wèi ordered Huì Shī to go to Chǔ,
and ordered Xī Shǒu to go to Qí.
Treating the two men equally,
with carriages of equal number,
he intended to test their diplomatic ties.
The King of Chǔ heard of this,
and Huì Shī therefore sent someone ahead to Chǔ,
saying:
"The King of Wèi has ordered Xī Shǒu to go to Qí,
and Huì Shī to go to Chǔ,
treating the two men equally,
intending to test their diplomatic ties."
The King of Chǔ heard this,
and therefore went to the outskirts to welcome Huì Shī.
King Huì of Wèi mobilized the troops from within his borders,
and, with Crown Prince Shēn, attacked Qí.
A guest said to the tutor of Prince Lǐ:
"Why not have the prince weep before the Queen Dowager,
to halt the Crown Prince's campaign?
If the matter succeeds, you will have established virtue;
if it does not succeed, you will become king.
The Crown Prince is young,
and unskilled in warfare.
Tián Bān is a seasoned general,
and Sūnzǐ excels in employing troops.
In battle, they are certain not to be victorious;
if not victorious, they are certain to be captured.
If the prince contends with the king over this,
and the king listens to the prince,
the prince will not be enfeoffed;
if the king does not listen to the prince,
the Crown Prince is sure to be defeated;
if defeated,
the prince is sure to be established;
once established,
he is sure to become king."
Qí and Wèi fought at Mǎlíng,
Qí achieved a great victory over Wèi,
killed Crown Prince Shēn,
and annihilated an army of one hundred thousand.
The King of Wèi summoned Huì Shī and told him:
"That Qí,
is my enemy,
a hatred I will not forget until death.
Though my state is small,
I constantly wish to raise all my troops and attack it.
What do you think?"
He replied:
"It cannot be done.
I have heard that
a true king attains proper measure,
while a hegemon understands strategy.
What Your Majesty has now told me
shows a lack of proper measure and distance from strategy.
Your Majesty originally first incurred enmity with Zhào,
and afterward fought with Qí.
Now, having been defeated in battle,
with the state lacking preparations for defense or offense,
Your Majesty again wishes to raise all troops and attack Qí.
This is not what I would call proper.
If Your Majesty wishes to take revenge on Qí,
then it would be better to change attire, humble yourself, and pay court to Qí.
The King of Chǔ will certainly be angered.
Your Majesty can then send agents to incite conflict between them,
and Chǔ will surely attack Qí.
Using a rested Chǔ to attack a weary Qí,
Qí is sure to be captured by Chǔ.
Thus, Your Majesty would use Chǔ to destroy Qí."
The King of Wèi said:
"Excellent."
He then sent a messenger to report to Qí,
expressing willingness to submit and pay court.
Tián Yīng agreed.
Zhāng Chǒu said:
"This cannot be done.
If we had not defeated Wèi in battle,
and yet received their courtly rites,
making peace with Wèi and thereby subduing Chǔ,
this would be a great victory.
But now we have defeated Wèi in battle,
annihilated an army of one hundred thousand,
and captured Crown Prince Shēn;
if we accept the submission of the mighty Wèi,
and thereby belittle Qín and Chǔ,
their violent resentment will certainly be settled upon us.
Moreover, the King of Chǔ is by nature
fond of using troops and greatly seeks fame;
in the end, the one who will bring calamity upon Qí
is sure to be Chǔ."
Tián Yīng did not listen,
and subsequently admitted the King of Wèi,
joining with him in repeatedly paying court to the Marquis of Qí.
The Zhào clan found this disgraceful.
The King of Chǔ was enraged,
personally led troops to attack Qí,
Zhào responded in support,
and they soundly defeated Qí at Xúzhōu.
Huì Shī worked to establish relations between Hán and Wèi,
and had Crown Prince Míng serve as a hostage in Qí.
The King wished to see him.
Zhū Cāng said to the King:
"Why not claim illness?
I request to persuade Yīngzǐ, saying:
'The King of Wèi is advanced in years,
and now is ill.
You, sir, would do better to return the Crown Prince to show him kindness.
Otherwise,
Prince Gāo is in Chǔ,
and Chǔ will likely install him as heir,
which would leave Qí holding an empty hostage and acting unjustly.'"
Tián Xū was esteemed by the King of Wèi.
Master Huì said:
"You must be good to those around you.
Consider the poplar tree:
plant it horizontally, and it grows;
plant it upside down, and it grows;
break it and plant it, and still it grows.
Yet if ten people plant poplars,
and one person uproots them,
then there will be no living poplars.
Therefore, with a group of ten people,
planting something easy to grow,
yet unable to overcome one person—
why is that?
Because planting is difficult, and removing is easy.
Now, though you have planted yourself with the king,
there are many who wish to remove you.
Then you are sure to be in danger."
Tián Xū died.
Zhāo Yú said to Sū Dài:
"Tián Xū has died.
I fear that one of
Zhāng Yí,
Lord Xuē,
or Xī Shǒu will become chancellor of Wèi."
Dài said:
"Then whom would you find suitable as chancellor?"
Zhāo Yú said:
"I wish for the Crown Prince to become chancellor himself."
Dài said:
"Allow me to go north to see the King of Liáng for you,
and he will surely be made chancellor."
Zhāo Yú said:
"How?"
Dài said:
"You play the part of the King of Liáng,
and I will try to persuade you."
Zhāo Yú said:
"How?"
He replied:
"I, Dài, have come from Chǔ,
and Zhāo Yú is very worried.
I said:
'Why are you worried?'
He said:
'Tián Xū has died,
and I fear that one of
Zhāng Yí,
Lord Xuē,
or Xī Shǒu will become chancellor of Wèi.'
I said:
'Do not worry.
The King of Liáng
is a wise ruler,
and will certainly not make Zhāng Yí chancellor.
If Zhāng Yí becomes chancellor of Wèi,
he will certainly favor Qín over Wèi.
If Lord Xuē becomes chancellor of Wèi,
he will certainly favor Qí over Wèi.
If Xī Shǒu becomes chancellor of Wèi,
he will certainly favor Hán over Wèi.
The King of Liáng,
being a wise ruler,
will certainly not allow them to become chancellor.'
I said:
'It would be best for the Crown Prince to become chancellor himself.
These three men all know that the Crown Prince would not be a permanent chancellor,
and each will strive to serve Wèi with the affairs of his own state,
hoping to obtain the chancellor's seal.
With Wèi's strength,
and the support of three ten-thousand-chariot states,
Wèi is sure to be secure.
Therefore, I say
it would be best for the Crown Prince to become chancellor himself.'"
He then went north to see the King of Liáng,
and reported these words to him.
The Crown Prince indeed became chancellor himself.
Qín summoned Lord Xìn'ān, the chancellor of Wèi,
but Lord Xìn'ān did not wish to go.
Sū Dài spoke on his behalf to the King of Qín, saying:
"I have heard that
loyalty does not necessarily mean compliance,
and compliance does not necessarily mean loyalty.
Now I wish to state my foolish opinion to Your Majesty,
but fear it may be seen as disloyal by your officials below,
bringing upon myself the crime of execution.
I beg Your Majesty to consider this.
Now, if Your Majesty sends someone to take charge of affairs in Wèi,
to perfect your relations, I fear it will only increase Wèi's suspicions of the relationship."
It is intended to block Zhào,
but I fear that Zhào will only grow stronger.
As for King Wèi's fondness and familiarity with Wèi Xìn,
it is profound;
his wisdom and ability to employ him,
are substantial;
his fear and aversion to the stern and respected Qín,
are clear.
Now, if Your Majesty sends someone into Wèi and he is not employed,
then Your Majesty's sending someone into Wèi is of no benefit.
If he is employed,
Wèi will certainly abandon the one they love and are familiar with and employ the one they fear and detest,
and this is why King Wèi will feel uneasy.
To abandon the affairs of a state of ten thousand chariots and withdraw,
this is what Wèi Xìn would find difficult to do.
To cause another state's ruler to be in an uneasy position,
and to cause another state's minister to do what he cannot,
to consider this as fostering closeness,
then it will be difficult to last long.
Therefore, I fear that the alliance with Wèi will become increasingly doubtful.
Moreover, if Wèi Xìn abandons his duties,
then the strategists of Zhào will surely say:
'If he abandons Qín,
Qín will certainly order its own beloved and trusted ones to be employed in Zhào.'
This would mean Zhào survives while we perish,
Zhào is secure while we are in danger.
Then above, there will be the spirit for field battles,
and below, the resolve to hold firm in defense,
therefore I fear that Zhào will only grow stronger.
"If Your Majesty wishes to preserve the alliance with Wèi,
and make Zhào cautious,
it would be better to employ Wèi Xìn and honor him with a title.
If Wèi Xìn serves Your Majesty,
his state will be secure and his name honored;
if he turns away from Your Majesty,
his state will be in danger and his power diminished.
Thus, in Wèi Xìn's service to his lord,
above, he will be loyal in serving his ruler,
below, he will act substantially for his own benefit,
his service to Your Majesty will certainly be complete.
The influential figures in Zhào will surely say:
'The reputation and lineage of the Wèi clan are not higher than ours,
the substance of their land is not richer than ours.
Wèi Xìn, by having Hán and Wèi serve Qín,
Qín treats him very well,
his state gains security,
and he himself attains honor.
Now we, by creating difficulties with Qín's troops and becoming a target,
place our state in a weakened and dangerous situation,
which is not a sound strategy.
To incur resentment abroad,
and bring worry to our ruler at home,
placing ourselves in a life-and-death situation, is not a complete course of action.'
They will lament their past actions,
and regret their mistaken conduct;
hoping for benefit,
they will certainly cede much land to deeply submit to Your Majesty.
Then, for Your Majesty, with folded arms and ease,
to obtain land ceded as substantial profit,
is something even Yáo and Shùn sought but could not obtain.
I wish Your Majesty to consider this."
The Siege of Píshì
Qín and
Chǔ attacked Wèi,
besieging Píshì.
Someone spoke to the King of Chǔ on behalf of Wèi, saying:
"If Qín and Chǔ defeat Wèi,
King Wèi's fear of seeing his state destroyed will be evident,
and he will certainly abandon himself to Qín.
Why does Your Majesty not turn against Qín and ally with King Wèi?
King Wèi will be pleased,
and will certainly send his crown prince as a hostage.
Qín, fearing to lose Chǔ,
will certainly offer cities and land to Your Majesty,
and then Your Majesty can again join them to attack Wèi."
The King of Chǔ said:
"Good."
Then he turned against Qín and allied with Wèi.
Wèi sent its crown prince to Chǔ as a hostage.
Qín grew fearful,
promised Chǔ cities and land, wishing to join them again to attack Wèi.
Chūlǐ Jí was angry,
and wanted to join Wèi to attack Chǔ,
but feared that Wèi, because its crown prince was in Chǔ, would not agree.
Someone spoke to the King of Chǔ on behalf of Jí, saying:
"The foreign minister Jí has sent me to present this:
he says:
'My humble ruler wishes to present cities and land,
but because the crown prince of Wèi is still in Chǔ,
he dares not do so.
If Your Majesty releases the Wèi hostage,
I request to present them,
and to reaffirm the alliance between Qín and Chǔ,
to swiftly attack Wèi.'"
The King of Chǔ said:
"Agreed."
Then he released the crown prince of Wèi.
Qín thereupon joined with Wèi to attack Chǔ.
Páng Cōng and the crown prince were hostages in Hándān,
and he said to the King of Wèi:
"Now if one person says there is a tiger in the market,
would Your Majesty believe it?"
The King said:
"No."
"If two people say there is a tiger in the market,
would Your Majesty believe it?"
The King said:
"I would doubt it."
"If three people say there is a tiger in the market,
would Your Majesty believe it?"
The King said:
"I would believe it."
Páng Cōng said:
"That there is no tiger in the market is clear,
yet three people saying so creates a tiger.
Now Hándān is farther from Dàliáng than the market,
and those who speak against me are more than three.
I hope Your Majesty will consider this."
The King said:
"I know it myself."
Thereupon he took his leave and departed,
but slanderous words arrived first.
Later, when the crown prince ended his hostage duty and returned,
he indeed was not granted an audience.
King Liáng, Wèi Yīng, feasted the feudal lords at Fántái.
When the wine was flowing freely,
he asked the Lord of Lǔ to raise his cup.
The Lord of Lǔ rose,
stepped away from his mat, and carefully spoke:
"In ancient times,
the emperor's daughter ordered Yí Dí to make wine, and it was delicious,
she presented it to Yǔ,
Yǔ drank and found it sweet,
then he distanced himself from Yí Dí,
and abstained from fine wine,
saying:
'Later generations will surely have those who lose their states because of wine.'
Duke Huán of Qí, at midnight, was not satisfied,
Yì Yá then fried, roasted, and grilled,
blended the five flavors and presented it to him,
Duke Huán ate and was full,
until dawn he did not wake,
and said:
'Later generations will surely have those who lose their states because of taste.'
Duke Wén of Jìn obtained Nán Zhī Wēi,
for three days he did not hold court,
then pushed Nán Zhī Wēi away and distanced himself from her,
saying:
'Later generations will surely have those who lose their states because of beauty.'
The King of Chǔ ascended Qiángtái and gazed upon the collapsing mountains,
with the river on the left and the lake on the right,
overlooking the wandering waters,
his joy made him forget death,
then he made a vow at Qiángtái not to ascend it again,
saying:
'Later generations will surely have those who lose their states because of high terraces and ponds
and pools.'
Now, the wine vessels of our host lord,
are the wine of Yí Dí;
the flavors of our host lord,
are the seasoning of Yì Yá;
with Báitái on the left and Lǘ Xū on the right,
are the beauty of Nán Wēi;
with Jiālín in front and Lántái behind,
are the joy of Qiángtái.
To have one of these,
is enough to lose one's state.
Now our host lord possesses all four,
can he not be warned!"
King Liáng repeatedly praised him.
Qín and Zhào made a pact to attack Wèi,
and King Wèi was troubled by this.
Máng Mǎo said:
"Your Majesty need not worry.
I request to send Zhāng Yǐ to tell the King of Zhào:
As for Yè,
I, your humble servant, originally do not possess it by right.
Now if Your Majesty joins with Qín to attack Wèi,
I request to serve Your Majesty with Yè."
The King of Zhào was pleased,
summoned his chancellor, and commanded him, saying:
"King Wèi requests to serve me with Yè,
and asks me to break with Qín."
The chancellor said:
"Joining with Qín to attack Wèi,
the benefit is no more than Yè.
Now without using troops we obtain Yè,
I request we agree to Wèi's offer."
Zhāng Yǐ then said to the King of Zhào:
"The officials of our humble state who are to hand over the city
are already in Yè.
How will Your Majesty repay Wèi?"
The King of Zhào then ordered the passes closed to sever relations with Qín.
Qín and Zhào became bitterly hostile.
Máng Mǎo responded to the Zhào envoy, saying:
"The reason our humble state serves Your Majesty
is to preserve Yè.
As for the ceding of Yè,
that was the fault of the envoy;
Mǎo knew nothing of it."
The King of Zhào, fearing that Wèi would take advantage of Qín's anger,
hastily ceded five cities to form an alliance with Wèi and resist Qín.
Máng Mǎo said to the King of Qín:
"Among Your Majesty's officers,
there is none who acts as an inside agent.
I have heard that an enlightened king does not proceed without an inside agent.
What Your Majesty desires from Wèi
are the lands of Chángyáng, Wángwū, and Luòlín.
If Your Majesty can have me appointed as Wèi's Minister of Education (Sītú),
then I can make Wèi offer them."
The King of Qín said:
"Good."
He then secured Máng Mǎo's appointment as Wèi's Minister of Education.
Máng Mǎo said to the King of Wèi:
"What Your Majesty worries about is the territory in the west.
What Qín desires from Wèi
are the lands of Chángyáng, Wángwū, and Luòlín.
If Your Majesty offers them to Qín,
then the western territory will have no worries.
Then we can request troops to go east and attack Qí,
and the land we seize will certainly be extensive."
The King of Wèi said:
"Good."
He then offered the lands to Qín.
Several months after the lands were handed over,
Qín's troops had not yet been dispatched.
The King of Wèi said to Máng Mǎo:
"The lands have been handed over for several months,
yet Qín's troops have not been dispatched.
Why is this?"
Máng Mǎo said:
"I deserve death for this crime.
However,
if I die,
the agreement with Qín will be broken,
and Your Majesty will have no means to hold Qín accountable.
If Your Majesty will pardon my crime,
I will go and hold Qín to the agreement on Your Majesty's behalf."
He then went to Qín
and said to the King of Qín:
"The reason Wèi offered the lands of Chángyáng, Wángwū,
and Luòlín
was with the intention of having Your Majesty's troops dispatched
to go east and attack Qí.
Now the lands have been handed over,
yet Qín's troops cannot be dispatched;
I am thus a dead man.
However,
hereafter, the gentlemen east of the mountains
will have no means to profitably serve Your Majesty."
The King of Qín, startled, said:
"The state has had matters to attend to,
and we have not yet been able to dispatch the troops.
Now we will send the troops to follow you."
Ten days later,
Qín's troops were dispatched.
Máng Mǎo jointly commanded the troops of Qín and Wèi
to go east and attack Qí,
opening up twenty-two counties of territory.
Qín defeated Wèi at Huá,
drove Máng Mǎo to flight, and besieged Dàliáng.
Xū Jiǎ, on behalf of Wèi, said to the Marquis of Ráng:
"I have heard that the great ministers and elders of the Wèi clan all said to the King of Wèi:
'In the beginning, King Huì attacked Zhào,
was victorious at Sānliáng,
and with an army of a hundred thousand captured Hándān.
The Zhào clan did not cede territory,
and Hándān was restored.
The men of Qí attacked Yān,
killed Zǐzhī,
and destroyed the old capital.
Yān did not cede territory,
and the state of Yān was restored.
The reason Yān and Zhào preserved their states intact with strong armies,
and their lands were not annexed by the feudal lords,
was because they were able to endure hardship
and valued not giving up territory.
Sòng and Zhōngshān were repeatedly attacked and repeatedly ceded territory,
and consequently perished.
I believe that Yān and Zhào can serve as models,
and Sòng and Zhōngshān as warnings.
Now Qín is a greedy and violent state without affection,
nibbling away at Wèi,
devouring the Jìn state.
It defeated Bào Zǐ,
and took eight counties.
Before the lands were fully handed over, its troops came out again.
How could Qín ever be satisfied!
Now it has again driven Máng Mǎo to flight,
and entered the northern territory.
This is not merely an attack on Dàliáng,
but also to coerce Your Majesty into ceding much territory.
Your Majesty must not listen.
If now Your Majesty follows Chǔ and Zhào in seeking peace,
Chǔ and Zhào, angered, will compete with Your Majesty in serving Qín,
and Qín is sure to accept them.
Qín, backed by the troops of Chǔ and Zhào, will attack again,
and then it will be impossible to save the state from destruction.
I hope Your Majesty will certainly not seek peace.
If Your Majesty does wish to seek peace,
you must cede little and have hostages;
otherwise, you will certainly be deceived.'
This is what I heard in Wèi,
and I hope you, sir, will consider matters accordingly.
"The *Zhōu Shū* says:
'Fate is not constant.'
This means that fortune cannot be counted on repeatedly.
Now, defeating Bào Zǐ
and taking eight counties—
this was not due to the excellence of military strength,
nor to the skill of strategy,
but largely to heavenly fortune.
Now, again driving Máng Mǎo to flight,
entering the northern territory,
and attacking Dàliáng—
this is to consider heavenly fortune as constant.
The wise do not act thus.
"I have heard that Wèi has mobilized the elite troops from all its hundred counties
to come and garrison Dàliáng.
I estimate them to be no fewer than three hundred thousand.
With a host of three hundred thousand
defending a city wall seventy feet high,
I believe that even if Tāng and Wǔ were reborn,
they would find it hard to attack.
To lightly trust in the troops of Chǔ and Zhào,
assault a seventy-foot-high wall,
and face a host of three hundred thousand,
yet be determined to take it—
I believe that from the beginning of the division of the world until now,
such a thing has never been.
If the attack fails and the city is not taken,
the Qín troops will certainly be exhausted,
Yīn will certainly be lost,
and all previous achievements will be abandoned.
Now Wèi is wavering;
you can secure it by ceding a little territory.
I hope that before the troops of Chǔ and Zhào have reached Dàliáng,
you will quickly secure it by ceding a little.
Wèi is wavering,
and if it can make peace by ceding a little,
it will certainly desire to do so.
Then you, sir, will achieve your desire.
Chǔ and Zhào will be angered that Wèi made peace before them,
and will certainly compete in serving Qín.
The alliance will thereby dissolve,
and you, sir, can choose later.
Moreover, when you, sir, previously took territory by partitioning the Jìn state,
why was it necessary to use troops?
Without using troops,
Wèi yielded Jiàng and Ānyì,
and also opened two opportunities for Yīn,
taking all of the former Sòng,
and Wèi yielded Yóudàn.
The Qín troops are already mobilized,
and you, sir, control them.
What can you not obtain?
What can you not accomplish?
I hope you, sir, will consider this carefully and not proceed dangerously."
The Marquis of Ráng said:
"Good."
He then lifted the siege of Dàliáng.
Qín defeated Wèi at Huá,
and the King of Wèi was about to go to court in Qín.
Zhōu Xīn said to the king:
"There was a man of Sòng who studied,
and after three years returned home and called his mother by her name.
His mother said:
'You studied for three years,
and upon returning call me by my name—
why is this?'
Her son said:
'Among those I consider worthy,
none surpass Yáo and Shùn,
and Yáo and Shùn are called by their names.'
What I consider great,
is nothing greater than Heaven and Earth,
thus they are named Heaven and Earth.
Now, a mother’s worthiness cannot surpass Yáo and Shùn,
and a mother’s greatness cannot surpass Heaven and Earth,
therefore, she is named ‘mother.’”
His mother said:
“As for you in your studies,
do you intend to fully practice them?
I wish you had something to replace the naming of ‘mother.’
As for you in your studies,
do you intend to not practice some of them?
I wish you would postpone the naming of ‘mother.’”
Now, regarding Your Majesty’s service to Qín,
is there still something that can replace going to court?
I wish Your Majesty had something to replace it,
and postpone going to court.”
King of Wèi said:
“Are you worried that I will enter and not return?
Xǔ Wǎn made an oath for me, saying:
‘If you enter and do not return,
I request to offer my head as a sacrifice for Your Majesty.’”
Zhōu Xīn replied:
“As lowly as I am,
if someone now told me,
to enter an unfathomable abyss and must return,
if I do not return,
he would offer a rat’s head as a sacrifice for me,
I certainly would not do it.
Now, Qín is an unpredictable state,
like an unfathomable abyss;
and Xǔ Wǎn’s head,
is like a rat’s head.
To place Your Majesty in the unpredictable Qín,
and sacrifice a rat’s head for Your Majesty,
I privately believe it is not advisable for Your Majesty.
Moreover, which is more urgent: losing Liáng or losing Hénèi?”
The King said:
“Losing Liáng is more urgent.”
“Which is more urgent: losing Liáng or losing your life?”
The King said:
“Losing my life is more urgent.”
He said:
“Among these three,
life,
is the highest;
Hénèi,
is the lowest.
Qín has not yet demanded the lowest,
yet Your Majesty offers the highest,
is this acceptable?”
The King still did not listen.
Zhī Qī said:
“Your Majesty, observe the King of Chǔ.
If the King of Chǔ enters Qín,
Your Majesty can go ahead with three carriages;
if the King of Chǔ does not enter,
Chǔ and Wèi united,
would still be sufficient to resist Qín.”
The King then stopped.
The King said to Zhī Qī:
“I have already promised Yìng Hóu,
not going now would be deceiving him.”
Zhī Qī said:
“Your Majesty, do not worry.
I will have Chángxìn Hóu
request that Your Majesty not enter,
Your Majesty, wait for me.”
Zhī Qī persuaded Chángxìn Hóu, saying:
“The King orders the summoning of the Prime Minister.”
Chángxìn Hóu said:
“Why does the King want me?”
Zhī Qī said:
“I do not know,
the King urgently summons you.”
Chángxìn Hóu said:
“When I urged the King to enter Qín,
was it for Qín’s sake?
It was for Wèi’s sake.”
Zhī Qī said:
“Do not plan for Wèi,
you should plan for yourself.
Do you prefer to die in peace?
Or live in peace?
Do you prefer poverty?
Or nobility?
You should first plan for yourself,
then plan for Wèi.”
Chángxìn Hóu said:
“Lord Lóu is about to enter,
I will follow now.”
Zhī Qī said:
“The King urgently summons you,
if you do not go,
blood will stain your robe!”
Chángxìn Hóu went,
Zhī Qī followed behind him.
About to see the King,
Zhī Qī entered first and said to the King:
“Pretend to be ill when you see him,
I have already frightened him.”
Chángxìn Hóu entered to see the King,
the King said:
“I am very ill, what can I do!
I have already promised Yìng Hóu,
even if I die on the way, should I go?”
Chángxìn Hóu said:
“Your Majesty, do not go!
I can persuade Yìng Hóu,
I wish Your Majesty not to worry.”
During the battle of Huá Jūn,
Wèi did not defeat Qín.
The following year,
they were about to send Duàngān Chóng to cede territory and negotiate peace.
Sūn Chén said to the King of Wèi:
“If Wèi does not cede territory after defeat,
it can be said to skillfully handle defeat;
and if Qín does not demand territory after victory,
it can be said to not know how to use victory.
Now, after a year, you want to cede territory,
this is the ministers’ private scheme, and Your Majesty does not know.
Moreover, the one who desires the seal,
is Duàngān Zǐ,
yet Your Majesty sends him to cede territory;
the one who desires territory,
is Qín,
yet Your Majesty sends him to receive the seal.
The one who desires the seal controls the territory,
and the one who desires territory controls the seal,
inevitably, Wèi will cease to exist.
Moreover, treacherous ministers all wish to serve Qín with territory.
To serve Qín with territory,
is like carrying firewood to extinguish a fire.
If the firewood is not exhausted,
the fire will not stop.
Now, Your Majesty’s territory is limited,
but Qín’s demands are endless,
this is the analogy of firewood and fire.”
The King of Wèi said:
“Good.
However,
I have already promised Qín,
it cannot be changed.”
He replied:
“Has Your Majesty not seen how the xiāo piece is used in the board game?
When it wants to eat, it eats;
when it wants to hold, it holds.
Now, Your Majesty is coerced by the ministers and promised Qín,
and thus says it cannot be changed,
why is Your Majesty’s wisdom not equal to the xiāo piece?”
The King of Wèi said:
“Good.”
Then he halted the action.
Qí wanted to attack Wèi,
Wèi sent someone to tell Chúnyú Kūn
saying: “Qí wants to attack Wèi,
only you, sir, can resolve Wèi’s crisis.
Our humble state has two pairs of precious jade disks,
and eight fine horses,
we ask to present them to you, sir.”
Chúnyú Kūn
said: “Agreed.”
He went to persuade the King of Qí, saying:
“Chǔ,
is Qí’s enemy;
Wèi,
is Qí’s ally.
To attack an ally,
and let the enemy take advantage of the remaining weakness,
is disgraceful in name and dangerous in reality,
I do not think it advisable for Your Majesty.”
The King of Qí said:
“Good.”
Then he did not attack Wèi.
A guest said to the King of Qí:
“Chúnyú Kūn advised against attacking Wèi
because he received Wèi’s jade disks and horses.”
The King said to Chúnyú Kūn
saying:
“I heard that you, sir, received Wèi’s jade disks and horses,
is this true?”
He said:
"Yes, there is."
"Then how would you advise me, sir?"
Chúnyú Kūn
said: "Attacking Wèi is not advantageous.
Even if Wèi were to assassinate me,
what benefit would that bring to Your Majesty?
If it is truly not advantageous,
even if Wèi were to enfeoff me, what loss would that bring to Your Majesty?
Moreover, Your Majesty would avoid the criticism of attacking an allied state,
Wèi would be spared the danger of imminent destruction,
the common people would be free from the calamity of war,
and I would gain the treasures of jade and horses—
what harm would that bring to Your Majesty?"
Qín was about to attack Wèi.
The King of Wèi heard of this,
and at night summoned Mèngcháng Jūn,
telling him:
"Qín is about to attack Wèi.
You must devise a plan for me—
what should be done?"
Mèngcháng Jūn said:
"If we have the rescue of the other feudal lords,
then the state can be preserved."
The king said:
"I wish for you to undertake this mission."
He heavily equipped him with a hundred chariots.
Mèngcháng Jūn went to Zhào,
and said to the King of Zhào:
"I, Wén, wish to borrow troops to rescue Wèi."
The King of Zhào said:
"I cannot do so."
Mèngcháng Jūn said:
"The reason I dare to borrow troops
is out of loyalty to Your Majesty."
The king said:
"May I hear your reasoning?"
Mèngcháng Jūn said:
"The troops of Zhào
are not necessarily stronger than those of Wèi;
the troops of Wèi
are not necessarily weaker than those of Zhào.
Yet Zhào's territory does not face annual peril,
and its people do not die annually;
while Wèi's territory faces annual peril,
and its people die annually—
why is this?
Because Wèi serves as a shield for Zhào in the west.
Now if Zhào does not rescue Wèi,
and Wèi forms a covenant with Qín,
then Zhào will share a border with powerful Qín.
Its territory will also face annual peril,
and its people will also die annually.
This is why I am loyal to Your Majesty."
The King of Zhào agreed,
and raised an army of one hundred thousand troops
and three hundred chariots.
He then went north to see the King of Yān, saying:
"Previously, the prince often pledged friendship between our two kings.
Now Qín is about to attack Wèi—
I hope Your Majesty will rescue it."
The King of Yān said:
"We have had poor harvests for two years now.
To march several thousand li now to aid Wèi—
how can that be done?"
Tián Wén said:
"To march several thousand li to rescue others
is to the benefit of the state.
If the King of Wèi were to step outside the capital gates and see the enemy army,
even if he wished to march several thousand li to aid others,
would it be possible?"
The King of Yān still had not agreed.
Tián Wén said:
"I offer Your Majesty a beneficial plan.
If Your Majesty does not adopt my loyal advice,
I shall take my leave.
I fear great changes are about to occur in the world."
The king said:
"May I hear about these great changes?"
He said:
"If Qín attacks Wèi but cannot conquer it,
its towers will already be burned,
and its hunting grounds already seized.
If Yān does not rescue Wèi,
the King of Wèi will humble himself and cede territory,
giving half his state to Qín,
and Qín will surely withdraw.
Once Qín has withdrawn from Wèi,
the King of Wèi will gather all the troops of Hán and Wèi,
and further borrow troops from Qín in the west,
joining with the masses of Zhào,
to attack Yān with four states' forces.
What benefit will Your Majesty have then?
Is it better to march several thousand li to aid others,
or to step outside Yān's southern gate and see the enemy army?
The distance is short and supplies are easy to transport—
what benefit will Your Majesty have?"
The King of Yān said:
"You may proceed.
I will heed your advice."
He then raised an army of eighty thousand troops
and two hundred chariots
to follow Tián Wén.
The King of Wèi was greatly pleased,
saying:
"You have obtained the troops of Yān and Zhào
in great numbers and with great speed."
The King of Qín was greatly alarmed,
and ceded territory to seek peace with Wèi.
He then returned the troops of Yān and Zhào,
and enfeoffed Tián Wén.
Wèi was about to join Qín in attacking Hán.
Zhū Jǐ said to the King of Wèi:
"Qín shares customs with the Róng and Dí tribes.
It has the heart of a tiger or wolf,
greedy, violent, fond of profit, and untrustworthy,
with no understanding of ritual, righteousness, virtue, or conduct.
If there is profit to be gained,
it disregards relatives and brothers,
like birds and beasts.
This is known throughout the world—
it is not a state that bestows generosity or accumulates virtue.
Thus, the Queen Dowager was its mother,
yet she died of grief;
the Marquis of Ráng was its uncle,
with achievements unsurpassed,
yet he was ultimately exiled;
its two younger brothers were innocent,
yet their states were seized again.
This is how it treats its own relatives and brothers—
how much more so with enemy states that are its foes?
Now Your Majesty joins Qín in attacking Hán, drawing closer to Qín.
I am deeply perplexed by this,
and if Your Majesty does not recognize it,
then you are not discerning.
If the ministers know it but none admonish you on this matter,
then they are not loyal.
Now the Hán clan, with a woman ruling a weak sovereign,
faces great internal turmoil—
how can it externally withstand the troops of powerful Qín and Wèi?
Does Your Majesty think it will not be defeated?
If Hán perishes,
Qín will possess all the territory of Zhèng,
bordering Dàliáng.
Does Your Majesty think that will be safe?
Your Majesty wishes to recover old territory,
but now you invite the calamity of powerful Qín.
Does Your Majesty think that is beneficial?
Qín is not a state that remains idle.
After Hán perishes,
it will surely seek further ventures;
seeking further ventures,
it will surely pursue what is easy and profitable;
pursuing what is easy and profitable,
it will surely not attack Chǔ or Zhào.
Why is this?
To cross mountains and rivers,
traverse Hán's Shàngdǎng to attack powerful Zhào—
that would repeat the events of Èyǔ,
and Qín will surely not do it.
If it takes the path of Hénèi,
passing by Yè and Zhāogē,
crossing the waters of Zhāng and Fǔ,
to engage Zhào's troops in decisive battle on the outskirts of Hándān—
that would invite the disaster of Zhì Bó,
and Qín would not dare.
To attack Chǔ,
passing through Shè Valley, traveling thirty li
to attack perilous and narrow passes—
the distance traveled is very far,
and the targets attacked are very difficult.
Qín would also not do it.
If it takes the path of Héwài,
with Dàliáng at its back,
and to the right, Shàngcài and Shàolíng,
to engage Chǔ's troops in decisive battle on the outskirts of Chén—
Qín would also not dare.
Therefore, it is said:
Qín will surely not attack Chǔ or Zhào,
nor will it attack Wèi or Qí.
After Hán perishes,
the day its troops march out,
there will be no target to attack but Wèi."
Qín already possesses the territories of Huáidì, Xíngqiū,
Zhīchéng, and Guǐjīn,
and from these positions, it threatens Hénèi.
The cities of Gòng and Jí in Hénèi are all in peril.
Qín holds the territory of Zhèng,
has captured Yuányōng,
and can breach the Yíngzé marsh,
flooding Dàliáng,
which would surely lead to the fall of Dàliáng.
Your Majesty’s envoy has committed a grave error
by slandering the Ānlíng clan to Qín,
for Qín has long coveted Xǔ.
However, Qín’s territories of Yèyáng
and Kūnyáng border Wǔyáng and Gāolíng.
Heeding the envoy’s slander,
Qín follows the Ānlíng clan’s lead and seeks to destroy it.
If Qín circles north of Wǔyáng
and advances eastward to threaten Xǔ,
then the southern state will certainly be endangered.
Even if the southern state is not endangered,
how could the state of Wèi remain secure?
Moreover, to resent Hán for not accepting the Ānlíng clan is acceptable,
but to not worry about Qín’s lack of concern for the southern state is a mistake.
In the past,
Qín was west of the Yellow River,
and the state of Jìn was distant from Liáng,
over a thousand lǐ away,
separated by mountains and rivers,
with Zhōu and Hán acting as buffers.
From the time of the Lín army to the present,
Qín has attacked Wèi ten times,
penetrating deep into the state five times,
with border cities all captured.
Wéntái was destroyed,
Chuídū was burned,
forests were felled,
deer were exterminated,
and the state was subsequently besieged.
Moreover, Qín advanced swiftly north of Liáng,
east to the outskirts of Táo and Wèi,
and north to Pínglǘ.
What was lost to Qín includes
Shānběi, Héwài, and Hénèi,
hundreds of large counties,
and dozens of major cities.
At that time, Qín was west of the Yellow River,
and the state of Jìn was still a thousand lǐ from Dàliáng,
yet the calamity was this severe.
How much worse would it be if Qín were to have no Hán but possess the territory of Zhèng,
with no mountains or rivers to block it,
no Zhōu or Hán to act as buffers,
and only a hundred lǐ from Dàliáng?
The calamity would certainly be a hundred times greater.
In the past,
alliances were not achieved,
and Chǔ and Wèi were suspicious, making it impossible to secure an alliance with Hán.
Now Hán has been under attack for three years.
Qín harasses it to force negotiations,
but Hán, knowing it faces destruction,
still refuses to yield,
sends hostages to Zhào,
and requests to lead the allied forces in battle.
In my view,
Chǔ and Zhào will certainly join in attacking Qín.
Why is this?
Because all know that Qín’s ambitions are boundless.
Unless it annihilates the armies of the world
and subjugates the people of the land,
it will never cease.
Therefore, I wish to serve Your Majesty,
urging you to quickly accept the alliance with Chǔ and Zhào,
secure hostages from Hán and Wèi,
make preserving Hán your priority,
and then demand the return of former territories from Hán.
Hán will certainly comply.
In this way, the people will not be burdened, and the former territories will be regained.
This achievement surpasses joining Qín in attacking Hán,
and you will avoid the calamity of bordering a powerful Qín.
"Preserving Hán and securing Wèi benefits the world,
and this is also a great opportunity for Your Majesty.
Connect Hán’s Shàngdǎng with Gòng and Mò,
and once the route is open,
establish a checkpoint there,
imposing tariffs on travelers,
which will make Hán’s Shàngdǎng a valuable hostage for Wèi.
Sharing the tariffs
will enrich the state,
and Hán will certainly be grateful, loyal, respectful, and fearful of Wèi,
and will never dare to rebel against Wèi.
Hán will then be like a county of Wèi.
If Wèi can treat Hán as a county,
then Wèi, Dàliáng, and Héwài will certainly be secure.
If Hán is not preserved now,
then the two Zhōu states will certainly be endangered,
and Ānlíng will certainly be lost.
Chǔ and Zhào will suffer great defeats,
Wèi and Qí will be deeply fearful,
and the world will turn westward and hasten to Qín,
with the day of submitting as vassals not far off."
Yèyángjūn made an agreement with Wèi,
and the King of Wèi intended to enfeoff his son.
He said to the King of Wèi:
"Your Majesty once crossed the Zhāng River,
paid homage in Hándān,
and ceded Gé, Bì, Yīn, and Chéng to Zhào as supporting territories,
yet Zhào has done nothing for Your Majesty.
Can Your Majesty now enfeoff his son with Wènyáng Gūyī?
I consider this inadvisable for Your Majesty."
The King of Wèi then halted the plan.
Qín instigated Zhào to attack Wèi.
Wèi said to the King of Zhào:
"Attacking Wèi
marks the beginning of Zhào’s downfall.
In the past,
the people of Jìn sought to destroy Yú by attacking Guó.
Attacking Guó
was the beginning of Yú’s downfall.
Thus, Xún Xī offered horses and jade to borrow a path through Yú.
Gōng Zhīqí advised against it, but his counsel was ignored,
and eventually, the path was granted to Jìn.
The people of Jìn attacked Guó
and on their return, seized Yú.
Therefore, the *Spring and Autumn Annals* recorded this,
condemning the Duke of Yú.
Today, no state is stronger than Zhào,
which rivals Qí and Qín.
Your Majesty is wise and has a renowned minister as chancellor,
yet the most critical threat to your state is Zhào itself.
Wèi is
Zhào’s Guó;
Zhào is
Wèi’s Yú.
Heeding Qín and attacking Wèi
is akin to Yú’s actions.
I hope Your Majesty will consider this carefully."
The crown prince of Wèi was in Chǔ.
He said to Lóuzǐ in Yānlíng:
"You must be waiting for Qí and Chǔ to ally
in order to rescue Píshì.
Given the current circumstances of Qí and Chǔ,
they will certainly not ally.
Those in the state who are hostile to Dízi
do not include you.
They all wish to ally Qí and Qín while alienating Chǔ to diminish your influence.
You must say to the King of Qí:
'Wèi’s being attacked
is not because Qín truly initiated the assault,
but because Chǔ resents Wèi’s service to Your Majesty,
and thus urged Qín to attack Wèi.'
The King of Qí already wishes to attack Chǔ,
and is angered that Chǔ is not friendly toward him,
so he will certainly order Wèi to cede territory to Qín and make peace.
With Zhāngzǐ’s strength
and the support of Qín and Hán,
the King of Qí resents him,
and the King of Wèi dares not rely on him.
Now, with the combined might of Qí and Qín,
alienating Chǔ to diminish your influence,
I fear for you.
If ceding territory
to make peace with Qín is inevitable,
would it not be better to do so through Chǔ?
If Qín fiercely attacks Chǔ,
and Chǔ withdraws its troops,
the King of Wèi will certainly be frightened.
You can then cede the area north of Fén to Qín to make peace,
ally with Chǔ to isolate Qí,
and Qín and Chǔ will value you,
ensuring you become chancellor.
I believe King of Qín and Chūlǐjí desire this,
and I request to persuade them on your behalf."
He then said to Chūlǐzǐ:
"Attacking Píshì
is the king’s primary task,
yet if it cannot be captured,
the world will look down on Qín.
Moreover, holding Píshì
is advantageous for attacking Hán and Wèi."
Chūlǐzǐ said:
"I have already made peace with Wèi,
so it is of no use."
The reply was:
"I wish to share my humble opinion with you,
and hope you will not take offense.
Holding Píshì
is greatly beneficial to the state,
yet you ceded it to Wèi
because you ultimately believed you could not hold it,
and thus gave it to Wèi.
Now, with your strength sufficient to hold it,
why not retain it?"
Chūlǐzǐ said:
"What should we do?"
He replied:
"What the King of Wèi relies on,
are Qí and Chǔ;
those he employs,
are Lóu and Dí Qiáng.
Now the King of Qí said to the King of Wèi:
'If you wish to negotiate an attack, using the pretext of Qí's troops,
this means you will not rescue us.'
The King of Chǔ is angry that Wèi does not employ Lóuzǐ,
and instead sends Dí Qiáng to make peace,
so his resentment has already severed relations.
The King of Wèi, fearing he will be destroyed,
Dí Qiáng wishes to ally with Qí and Qín, excluding Chǔ,
to diminish Lóu;
Lóu wishes to ally with Qín and Chǔ, excluding Qí,
to diminish Dí Qiáng.
You, sir, should mediate Wèi's peace negotiations,
and send someone to tell Lóuzǐ:
'Can you give me the area north of Fén?
I request to ally with Chǔ, excluding Qí,
to enhance your importance,
this is my affair.'
Lóuzǐ and the King of Chǔ will certainly act swiftly.
Then tell Dízǐ:
'Can you give me the area north of Fén?
I will certainly ally with Qí, excluding Chǔ,
to enhance your importance.'
Dí Qiáng and the King of Qí will certainly act swiftly.
Thus, externally you gain Qí and Chǔ for your use,
internally you gain Lóu and Dí Qiáng as your assistants,
why then can you not possess land east of the Yellow River?"
A memorial presented to the King of Qín said:
"I have previously heard that Your Majesty plans to take action against Liáng,
but I fear this plan is not well-considered,
I hope Your Majesty will deliberate on it carefully.
Liáng,
is the strategic point of Shāndōng.
There is a snake here,
strike its tail,
its head rescues it;
strike its head,
its tail rescues it;
strike its middle, head and tail both rescue it.
Now the King of Liáng,
is the middle of the world.
If Qín attacks Liáng,
this shows the world you aim to sever the spine of Shāndōng,
this is when Shāndōng's head and tail will both rescue the middle.
Shāndōng, seeing it will be destroyed, will certainly fear,
fear will certainly lead to a great alliance,
Shāndōng is still strong,
I see Qín's great troubles will surely arrive soon.
I humbly plan for Your Majesty,
it would be better to march south.
Take action in the south,
their troops are weak,
the world will certainly not rescue them,
territory can be expanded,
the state can be enriched,
troops can be strengthened,
the ruler can be honored.
Has Your Majesty not heard of Tāng's campaign against Jié?
He tested it by attacking the weak Mìxūshì as military training,
after conquering Mìxūshì, Tāng subdued Jié.
Now Qín is at enmity with Shāndōng,
if you do not first use the weak as military training,
your troops will certainly suffer great setbacks,
the state will certainly face great troubles."
Qín indeed attacked south, taking Lántián, Yān, and Yǐng.
In the eighth year,
he said to the King of Wèi:
"In the past, Cáo relied on Qí and despised Jìn,
Qí attacked Lí and Jǔ, and the people of Jìn destroyed Cáo.
Zēng relied on Qí to resist Yuè,
when Qí's Hézǐ caused turmoil, the people of Yuè destroyed Zēng.
Zhèng relied on Wèi and despised Hán,
when they attacked Yúguān, the Hán clan destroyed Zhèng.
Yuán relied on Qín and Dí and despised Jìn,
when Qín and Dí had a great famine, the people of Jìn destroyed Yuán.
Zhōngshān relied on Qí and Wèi and despised Zhào,
when Qí and Wèi attacked Chǔ, Zhào destroyed Zhōngshān.
These five states were destroyed,
all because of what they relied on.
Not only these five states are like this,
all destroyed states in the world are like this.
There are many reasons why a state cannot be relied upon,
its changes are innumerable.
Some because governance and education are not cultivated,
upper and lower are not harmonious,
and thus cannot be relied upon;
some because of worries from neighboring states,
and thus cannot be relied upon;
some because harvests fail,
stores are exhausted,
and thus cannot be relied upon;
some are changed by profit,
compared with calamity.
I therefore know a state cannot necessarily be relied upon.
Now you rely on Chǔ's strength,
and believe Chūnshēnjūn's words,
using this to confront Qín,
but the future is uncertain.
If Chūnshēnjūn changes,
you alone will suffer Qín's harm.
You possess a state of ten thousand chariots,
yet you make one man's will your command.
I consider this incomplete,
I hope you will deliberate on it carefully."
The King of Wèi asked Zhāng Máo:
"I wish to join Qín in attacking Hán, what do you think?"
Zhāng Máo replied: "Will Hán sit and wait for destruction?
Or will it cede territory and follow the world?"
The King said:
"Hán will cede territory and follow the world."
Zhāng Máo said:
"Does Hán resent Wèi?
Or resent Qín?"
The King said:
"Resent Wèi."
Zhāng Máo said:
"Is Hán stronger than Qín?
Or stronger than Wèi?"
The King said:
"Stronger than Qín."
Zhāng Máo said:
"Will Hán cede territory and follow the stronger,
and the one it does not resent?
Or cede territory and follow the not stronger,
and the one it resents?"
The King said:
"Hán will cede territory and follow the stronger,
and the one it does not resent."
Zhāng Máo said:
"The matter of attacking Hán,
you already understand."
A guest said to Sīmǎ Shíjī:
"To think for long that the world can be unified,
is to not know the world.
To want Wèi alone to resist Qín,
is to not know Wèi.
To say this gentleman does not know these two,
is to not know this gentleman.
Yet this gentleman advocates the vertical alliance,
what is his reasoning?
If the alliance succeeds, this gentleman gains importance,
if it fails, this gentleman loses importance,
this gentleman's position of importance,
is not based on reality.
Why do you not quickly, while the three states are still firm,
sell yourself to Qín,
Qín will certainly accept you.
Otherwise,
the horizontal alliance advocates will plot to use you to ally with Qín,
this is taking your resources,
to aid your enemy."
Wèi and Qín attacked Chǔ,
the King of Wèi was unwilling.
Lóu Huǎn said to the King of Wèi:
"If you do not join Qín in attacking Chǔ,
Chǔ will join Qín in attacking you.
You should let Qín and Chǔ fight,
and you control both."
Ránghóu attacked Dàliáng,
captured Běiyǐng,
the King of Wèi was about to submit.
Someone said to Ránghóu:
"You attacked Chǔ and obtained Wǎn and Ráng to expand Táo,
attacked Qí and obtained Gāng and Bó to expand Táo,
obtained Xǔ and Yānlíng to expand Táo,
the King of Qín did not question,
why?
Because Dàliáng had not yet fallen.
Now if Dàliáng falls,
Xǔ and Yānlíng will certainly be discussed,
discussed then you will certainly be cornered.
For your sake,
not attacking is better."
Bái Guī said to Xīnchéngjūn:
"A night traveler can avoid wrongdoing,
but cannot stop dogs from barking at him.
Thus I can avoid criticizing you before the King,
but cannot stop others from criticizing me before you."
Qín attacked Hán's Guǎn,
and the King of Wèi dispatched troops to rescue it.
Zhāo Jì said:
"Qín is a powerful state,
and Hán and Wèi share a border.
If it does not launch an attack, then all is well;
but if it does attack,
it will certainly be either Hán or Wèi.
Now, fortunately, it is Hán—
this is Wèi's good fortune.
If Your Majesty rescues it,
the place that will be relieved of the attack
will surely be Hán's Guǎn;
the place that will draw the attack
will surely be Wèi's Liáng."
The King of Wèi did not listen,
saying:
"If we do not take this opportunity to rescue Hán,
Hán will resent Wèi;
it will ally with Qín in the west,
and if Qín and Hán unite as one,
then Wèi will be in danger."
Thereupon, he rescued it.
Qín indeed abandoned Guǎn and attacked Wèi.
The King of Wèi was greatly alarmed
and said to Zhāo Jì:
"I did not follow your plan, and now disaster has come—
what should be done about it?"
Zhāo Jì then went on his behalf to see the King of Qín, saying:
"Your servant has heard that when an enlightened ruler listens to advice,
he does not allow personal bias to govern his policies—
this is the way to act with impartiality.
I hope Your Majesty will not attack Wèi
and will heed your servant."
The King of Qín said:
"Why?"
Zhāo Jì said:
"The alliances east of the mountains
sometimes unite and sometimes break apart—
why is that?"
The King of Qín said:
"I do not know."
He said:
"The reason the states of the world unite
is because Your Majesty's intentions are not certain;
the reason they break apart
is because Your Majesty's intentions are certain.
Now, attacking Hán's Guǎn
has put that state in danger,
and before the campaign is even concluded, you shift troops to Liáng—
there is no better way to unite the alliances of the world.
They will believe that Qín's demands
are certainly impossible to withstand.
Therefore, in planning for Your Majesty,
it would be better to align with Zhào.
Once Qín has subdued Zhào,
then Yān will not dare not serve Qín,
and Jīng and Qí will be unable to maintain their alliance alone.
If the world competes to oppose Qín,
then it will be weakened."
The King of Qín then stopped.
Qín and Zhào became embroiled in conflict and fought.
He said to the King of Wèi:
"It would be better to align with Qí and Zhào and then provoke Qín.
If Your Majesty does not provoke Zhào,
Zhào will not be destroyed by the provocation;
but if you provoke Qín,
Zhào will certainly fight again
and will certainly value Wèi highly.
This is a way to control both Qín and Zhào.
If Your Majesty wishes, you can ally with Qí and Zhào to attack Jīng;
if you wish, you can ally with Jīng and Zhào to attack Qí—
Your Majesty may await the opportunity to expand eastward."
During the Battle of Chángpíng,
Píngdū Jūn advised the King of Wèi:
"Why does Your Majesty not form an alliance?"
The King of Wèi said:
"Qín has promised me Yuányōng."
Píngdū Jūn said:
"Your servant believes Yuányōng is an empty grant."
The King of Wèi said:
"What do you mean?"
Píngdū Jūn said:
"Qín and Zhào have long been locked in a stalemate at Chángpíng with no resolution.
If the world sides with Qín,
then Zhào will cease to exist;
if it sides with Zhào,
then Qín will cease to exist.
Qín fears that Your Majesty will change sides,
so it uses Yuányōng as bait for Your Majesty.
If Qín defeats Zhào,
would Your Majesty dare demand the cession of Yuányōng?
Your Majesty would say,
'I dare not.'
If Qín does not defeat Zhào,
can Your Majesty make Hán cede Yuányōng?
Your Majesty would say,
'I cannot.'
Therefore, your servant says
that Yuányōng is an empty grant."
The King of Wèi said:
"Well said."
Lóu Wú arranged a meeting between Qín and Wèi,
intending to have the King of Qín meet at the border.
He said to the King of Wèi:
"If you meet without a minister accompanying you,
Qín will certainly appoint a minister.
If you do not accept this,
then relations with Qín will turn hostile;
if you accept it,
then hereafter your ministers
will all strive to serve those feudal lords who can give orders above Your Majesty.
Moreover, meeting with Qín and having a minister serve Qín
means losing Qí,
and Qín will certainly look down on Your Majesty's strength.
If you have Qí,
it would be better to appoint a minister from there.
Qí will certainly be pleased,
and thus, having Yōng, you meet with Qín—
Qín will certainly value Your Majesty highly."
Ruì Sòng wanted to sever the relations between Qín and Zhào,
so he had Wèi seize the land in Qín that supported the Queen Dowager of Qín.
Ruì Sòng said to the King of Qín:
"Wèi offered its state to Your Majesty,
but Your Majesty did not accept it,
so it offered its state to Zhào instead.
Lǐ Hǎo said to me:
'You claim to have no ties with Qín,
yet you support the Queen Dowager of Qín with land—
this is deceiving me,
so my humble state has seized it.'"
The King of Qín was enraged
and thereupon severed relations with Zhào.
On behalf of Wèi, he said to the King of Chǔ:
"If you demand an attack on Wèi from Qín,
Qín will certainly not heed Your Majesty.
This will leave your wisdom exhausted by Qín
and your relations with Wèi strained.
If Chǔ and Wèi bear grudges against each other,
then Qín's importance will increase.
Therefore, Your Majesty should instead follow the trend of the world,
attack Qí,
and exchange territory with Wèi.
Your troops will not be harmed,
your relations will not change,
and what you desire will certainly be obtained."
Guǎn Bí ordered Dí Qiáng to handle affairs with Qín.
He said to the King of Wèi:
"The relationship between Bí and Qiáng
is like that between a person from Jìn and a person from Chǔ.
When a person from Jìn sees a person from Chǔ in a hurry,
he buckles his sword and slows down;
the person from Chǔ dislikes his slowness and hurries even more.
Now, when Bí enters Qín's guest lodgings,
the lodgings are insufficient to accommodate him.
When Qiáng enters,
there is no one in Qín to shield him.
Qiáng
is Your Majesty's esteemed minister,
yet Qín treats him so poorly—
how can this be acceptable?"
Chéngyáng Jūn wanted to make Hán and Wèi submit to Qín,
but the King of Wèi saw no benefit in it.
Bái Guī said to the King of Wèi:
"Your Majesty should secretly send someone to persuade Chéngyáng Jūn, saying:
'If you enter Qín,
Qín will certainly detain you
and use you to extract more territory from Hán.
If Hán does not comply,
Qín will certainly detain you
and attack Hán.
Therefore, it would be better for you to proceed calmly and seek a hostage from Qín.'
Chéngyáng Jūn will certainly not enter Qín,
and Qín and Hán will not dare to unite—
then Your Majesty's importance will increase."
Qín captured Níngyì,
and the King of Wèi sent someone to tell the King of Qín:
"If Your Majesty returns Níngyì,
I will be the first in the world to seek an alliance."
Someone said to the King of Wèi:
"Your Majesty should not listen.
The King of Wèi sees that the world cannot be relied upon,
so he wants to seek an alliance first.
Those who have lost Níngyì
should cede two Níngyì to seek an alliance;
those who have gained Níngyì—
how could they possibly return Níngyì?"
Qín withdrew from Hándān,
attacked Wèi,
and captured Níngyì.
Wú Qìng, fearing that the King of Wèi would form an alliance with Qín,
said to the King of Wèi:
"When Qín attacks Your Majesty,
does Your Majesty know the reason?
All under heaven say it is because Your Majesty is close to Qín.
If Your Majesty were not close to Qín,
Qín would withdraw.
All say it is because Your Majesty is weak.
Your Majesty is not weaker than the two Zhōu states.
The Qín people left Hándān,
passed by the two Zhōu states, and attacked Your Majesty,
because they consider Your Majesty easy to control.
Does Your Majesty also know that weakness invites attack?"
The King of Wèi intended to attack Hándān.
Jì Liáng heard of this,
turned back midway,
with his clothes wrinkled and unkempt,
and dust on his head uncleaned,
went to see the king and said:
"On my way here just now,
I saw a man on the main road,
facing north while holding his reins,
who told me:
'I wish to go to Chǔ.'
I said:
'Since you are going to Chǔ,
why are you facing north?'
He said: 'My horses are excellent.'
I said:
'Though your horses are excellent,
this is not the road to Chǔ.'
He said:
'My funds are ample.'
I said: 'Though your funds are ample,
this is not the road to Chǔ.'
He said:
'My driver is skilled.'
'The more excellent these conditions are,
the farther you will be from Chǔ.'
Now Your Majesty, in every move, desires to become a hegemon and king,
and in every action, seeks to be trusted by all under heaven.
Relying on the greatness of Your Majesty's state,
the精锐 of its troops,
and attacking Hándān,
to expand territory and enhance reputation—
the more frequently Your Majesty acts,
the farther you will be from becoming a true king.
It is just like going to Chǔ by heading north."
Zhōu Xiào said to Gōng Tuō:
"For my sake, tell the King of Qí that
I, Xiào, am willing to serve as an external minister.
Have Qí support me in Wèi."
Gōng Tuō said: "That will not do,
for it shows Qí that you are of little importance.
Qí does not harm those who have Wèi's support for the sake of those who lack it.
Therefore, you would do better to show that you have Wèi's backing.
You should say:
'Whatever the king seeks from Wèi,
I will request Wèi to comply.'
Then Qí is sure to support you,
for then you will have Qí's backing,
and with Qí, you will have Wèi's support."
Zhōu Zuì was on good terms with Qí,
while Dí Qiáng was on good terms with Chǔ.
These two men
wished to harm Zhāng Yí in Wèi.
Zhāng Yí heard of this,
and thus had his man serve as the steward in charge of audiences, to monitor those granted audiences,
so that no one dared to harm Zhāng Yí.
Zhōu Zuì went to Qí.
The King of Qín was angered,
and ordered Yáo Jiǎ to reprimand the King of Wèi.
The King of Wèi, on his behalf, said to the King of Qín:
"The reason Wèi has been able to maintain relations with all under heaven for Your Majesty
is because of Zhōu Zuì.
Now Zhōu Zuì has abandoned me and gone to Qí,
so Qí will no longer have access to all under heaven.
My humble state's service to Your Majesty
will also no longer be burdened by Qí.
If Your great state wishes to hasten military action,
then simply press Zhào."
Qín and Wèi were allied states.
Qí and Chǔ made a pact and intended to attack Wèi.
Wèi sent envoys to seek aid from Qín,
with carriages and caps in constant sight along the road,
yet Qín's rescue did not come forth.
There was a man of Wèi named Táng Jū,
over ninety years old,
who said to the King of Wèi:
"This old minister requests to go west and persuade Qín,
so that troops may set out before I return—is that acceptable?"
The King of Wèi said: "Very well."
Then he prepared a carriage and sent him off.
Táng Jū met with the King of Qín.
The King of Qín said:
"You, venerable sir, have come all this way in distress,
which must have been very arduous.
Wèi has come seeking aid many times,
and I am well aware of Wèi's urgency."
Táng Jū replied:
"Since Your Majesty already knows of Wèi's urgency yet rescue has not arrived,
it means Your Majesty's ministers in charge of planning are incompetent.
Moreover, Wèi is a state of ten thousand chariots,
which calls itself an eastern vassal,
